notes: The flanged open-ended rectangular waveguide by FDTD over the single-mode band (HANDOVER section 6, item 11). Each run is otahub.num.horn_fdtd.sectoral_horn(a, b, a, b, 0.0, cells_per_lambda=N, guide_len, margin, npml, periods, flange=True): a guide a x b (wavelengths) from a back short, TE10 launched a quarter guide wavelength in front of it, an infinite PEC flange in the aperture plane, and the far field of the aperture plane's own E alone (BoxTransform k_plane: M = -z x E imaged through the flange - exact for a flange, so the box's size does not enter). a = 2p/N and b = 2q/N exactly: p and q whole cells across the half guide, so no guide is rounded onto the grid. fdtd_dbi is the boresight directivity; te10_dbi is the TE10 aperture (cos(pi x/a) across a, uniform across b) in an infinite ground plane at the same a, b, integrated by tests/test_open_ended_waveguide._direct, independently of the spec's fit (which it matches to 0.002 dB). Families: A b/a = 4/9 (the WR-90 family), B 1/2, C 0.3, D 0.6 (the spec's limits) - surveyed; E 0.4, G 0.45, F 0.55 - held out of the fit. Kinds: survey and holdout at 36 (A, B) or 40 (C-G) cells across a; grid - the same guides on 54-144 cells across a; coarse - 18 and 24 cells across a, recorded for the order of convergence and not fitted; margin, npml, periods, guide - one setting changed from base_settings (margin 0.7, npml 20, periods 50, guide_len 2.5), of which the margin, absorber and ring-down moved no run more than 0.000004 dB and the guide length 0.00012 dB. The -cut runs (a/lambda 0.507-0.514) have guide_len 2.5 and periods 50: the guide wavelength is 4-6 wavelengths there and the quarter-wave source would otherwise sit at the aperture. seconds is the wall time of the run on a shared 8-core laptop. The grid is what matters: at a fixed guide 36 cells across a reach 0.8 of the continuum excess and 72 cells 0.9, converging at an order rising from 1.09 (18-36-72 cells across a) to 1.18 (36-72-144) - the r^-1/3 field at the broad walls' edges - so the fit carries a grid term and F is the continuum. The record in fdtd_farfield.json ('oewg', 40-56 cells a wavelength) read +0.17 dB on three grids only because b/a changed with the grid (0.467, 0.444, 0.429) and cancelled the refinement; its N = 48 run is A-p18q8-N48 here, bit for bit, and the fit with its grid term reproduces all three to 0.0003 dB.
call: otahub.num.horn_fdtd.sectoral_horn(a, b, a, b, 0.0, cells_per_lambda=N, guide_len=guide_len, margin=margin, npml=npml, periods=periods, flange=True)

fit.model: fdtd_dbi - te10_dbi = F(x, y) + h**order * (G[0] + G[1] x + G[2] y/x), x = a/lambda, y = b/lambda, h = 1/N (cells per wavelength); least squares over the survey and grid runs (all with 36 or more cells across a). F, the excess in the continuum, is what the spec would carry; the h term is the grid's error.
fit.order_note: The finest grid triples give 1.18 (a/lambda 1, 36-72-144 cells across a) and 1.21 (0.818, 66-88-132); order_band_db is the range of F - F(order 1.2) over the domain when the whole fit is redone at another order.
fit.uncertainty_note: F to +-0.005 dB: the order (1.1 to 4/3: +0.003/-0.0033) and the fit's own worst residual (0.002, at a/lambda 1, b/a 0.6, where the excess turns over fastest). The settings checks contribute 0.0001, the far-field quadrature under 0.00001.

modal_check.notes: INDICATIVE - an independent full-wave model, not in the tests' computations: mode matching of the same flanged aperture (Galerkin on the guide modes of TE10's symmetry - m odd, n even - with cutoff wavenumber up to kc wavenumbers, against the half space's spectral admittance; power in = power through the aperture = far-field power to 1e-6). It converges slowly from below, the aperture edges again; delta is its excess over its own TE10 term, extrapolated_db at first order in 1/kc from kc 24 and 32. gamma is the TE10 reflection at the aperture.

proposal.what: directivity_dbi of specs/horn.json open_ended_waveguide becomes the TE10 aperture plus F, the flanged guide's own excess; the domain gate and the TE10 polynomial are unchanged. directivity_expr is the full replacement expression; excess_expr is F alone in the spec's variables.
proposal.notes_directivity_dbi: SOLVED: the flanged guide itself, over the single-mode band. The TE10 aperture (E across b, cos(pi x/a) across a) in an infinite ground plane - its pattern integrated over the hemisphere, and independently as a grid of magnetic dipoles through the exact planar power kernel (otahub.arrays), the two within 0.003 dB, fitted over a/lambda 0.5-1 and b/a 0.3-0.6 to 0.04% - plus what a full-wave FDTD of the guide in an infinite flange finds above it (otahub.num.horn_fdtd.sectoral_horn, flange=True: the far field of the aperture plane's own E imaged through the flange, exact for a flange): 0.06 dB near cutoff rising to 0.17-0.31 dB, more for a taller guide, whose excess peaks before a/lambda = 1 once b/a passes 0.42 (at 0.87 for b/a 0.6). It is the r^-1/3 field at the broad walls' edges and the evanescent modes the flange excites, which a pure TE10 aperture leaves out. From 132 runs over a/lambda 0.51-1 at b/a 0.3, 4/9, 1/2 and 0.6 (tests/data/oewg_flange_fdtd.json), every guide a whole number of cells: box, absorber, ring-down and guide length move it under 0.0002 dB; the grid does not - 36 cells across a reach 0.8 of it, 72 cells 0.9, at an order of 1.1-1.2 - so it is extrapolated to the continuum jointly with its cubic in a/lambda and b/lambda: 0.002 dB worst on 103 runs, 0.0005 on 9 guides held out (b/a 0.4, 0.45, 0.55), +-0.003 dB for the order. A mode-matching model of the same aperture converges toward it from below (0.1423 against 0.1423 dB at a/lambda 0.6, b/a 4/9; within 0.003 dB at 0.75 and 1). WR-90 has 5.97 dBi at 8.2 GHz, 6.52 at 10 and 7.33 at 12.4 - 0.15, 0.21 and 0.25 dB above the TE10 aperture's 5.82, 6.31 and 7.08. An earlier record of +0.17 dB at 10 GHz on three grids compared guides whose b/a changed with the grid, which cancelled the refinement; one before it (+0.48 dB) cut its transform box through the flange. This spec once carried (8/pi^2) 4 pi a b/lambda^2 - 2.48, 4.20 and 6.07 dBi - the large-aperture limit, which vanishes for a small aperture; it was 1.3-3.5 dB low.
proposal.notes_effective_to_physical_area: Effective aperture over physical, D/(4 pi A/lambda^2): 1.38 for WR-90 at 10 GHz, 1.81 at 8.2. Above 1 on a small aperture, which collects from more than its own area; it falls toward the taper efficiency 8/pi^2 as the aperture grows. (Named so because it is not an efficiency bounded by 1. This spec's 'aperture_efficiency' was 8/pi^2 whatever the size.)
proposal.notes_gain_dbi: Directivity with the guide lossless and the aperture's reflection neglected - so optimistic by the mismatch loss: |Gamma| 0.19-0.24 for a flanged WR-family guide at a/lambda 0.6-1, 0.16-0.26 dB (mode matching, indicative), and more toward cutoff.
validity: single-mode TE10 operation: f0 between the TE10 and TE20 cutoffs
aperture reflection is neglected, so the gain figure is optimistic by the mismatch loss (0.16-0.26 dB for a flanged guide at a/lambda 0.6-1, more toward cutoff)
an infinite flange is assumed; a bare guide end, or a finite flange, radiates backward as well and reads lower
directivity is solved for a guide in an infinite flange over a/lambda 0.5-1 and b/a 0.3-0.6 (FDTD runs from a/lambda 0.507); NaN outside
